name: PLIBERSEK, the Hon. Tanya Joan

headline.note: Pre-parliament UTS student-association, NSW Domestic Violence Unit and senator-staff work is documented, but dates and full-time status remain unresolved. Follow-up records conflicting study/work sequences, government-unit history and concurrent 2020 book editing with unknown pay and workload. No public/private full-time total is supportable; book publication and election dates are not employment endpoints.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts in Communications (Honours) student
career_spells.evidence_note: UTS records completion of the honours degree in 1993. The start date, study load and overlap with Women's Officer duties are not established.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament lists Women's Officer; Plibersek and the Australian Women's Register identify the UTS Students' Association role while she studied, including campaigning on campus safety and sexual harassment. Appointment dates, pay, hours and legal employment status are unresolved. A 2014 interview describes one year after the arts degree, while other accounts place the elected role during study. This may reflect undergraduate/honours sequencing but is unresolved; no start year, pay or full-time interval is invented.
career_spells.counting_note: Student-association work is classified as nonprofit and excluded; the available sources do not prove substantive paid full-time employment.

career_spells.role: Master of Politics and Public Policy student
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and member biographies establish the degree; the ALP biography says it was studied while Plibersek worked in the NSW Domestic Violence Unit. Enrolment, completion, load and overlap dates are unresolved. The Women’s Agenda introduction reverses the study/work sequence relative to the ALP and Evatt biographies. Preserve the discrepancy pending university or appointment records.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: NSW Ministry for the Status and Advancement of Women, Domestic Violence Unit
career_spells.role: Domestic violence researcher and publications creator / policy and research officer
career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament and Plibersek identify the NSW government unit. The ALP biography places it after graduation and during her master's study; ABC describes domestic-violence policy and research before her move to Senator Bruce Childs' staff. A February2009 South Sydney Herald profile records work for the NSW Department for Women as a domestic-violence researcher and creator of publications, followed by joining Senator Bruce Childs' staff. Exact payroll title, employing department, appointment and cessation dates, hours and leave are unresolved. Australia’s CEDAW report traces the unit’s formation in March1993 within the Women’s Coordination Unit and subsequent Ministry location. This confirms organisational context, not her personal appointment date.
career_spells.counting_note: Government control is clear, but missing dates and full-time evidence prevent a public-sector duration calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament lists electorate-officer work. The Australian Women's Register and ABC identify Senator Bruce Childs as the first parliamentary employer after the Domestic Violence Unit. Appointment dates, payroll title, hours, leave and transition to George Campbell are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Biographical sources place Campbell after Childs and describe research-officer duties. Start date, payroll title, hours, leave and campaign overlap remain unresolved. Election day has been removed as an unsupported employment cessation date.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Status of Women Committee and Economics Committee member; State Conference delegate
career_spells.evidence_note: Parliament records Status of Women Committee membership from 1994 to 1998, Economics Committee membership from 1996 to 1998 and State Conference delegation from 1996 to 2004. Pay and workload are not stated; part of the interval follows election to Parliament.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Sydney
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster, current Parliament profile and Australian Government Directory establish continuous House service from 3 October 1998. The June2007 Procedure Committee report records approved House maternity leave6February–5April2001 and8February–17March2005. These are parliamentary attendance-leave periods within continuing elected service, not proof of zero constituency work, unpaid leave, a break in membership or nonparliamentary employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: NewSouth / UNSW Press (publisher; employment or contracting relationship unresolved)
career_spells.role: Editor, Upturn: A better normal after COVID-19
career_spells.evidence_note: Publisher credits her as editor of the book published November 2020; UTS launch corroborates the work. Publication date is not the editing interval. Remuneration, royalties, contract, workload and breaks unknown; concurrent with elected office. The original 47th-Parliament disclosure declares personal royalties from an unnamed publication, donated equally to two charities. This establishes disclosed publication income, but does not name Upturn or identify its contract/remuneration. Do not attribute those royalties specifically to this editing project, convert receipt into work dates or assume full-time labour.
career_spells.counting_note: Publication is not proof of paid full-time employment or university employment. No sector duration calculated.

career_spells.evidence_note: Original parliamentary disclosure section2(ii) lists her personally as trustee of the charitable trust, which awards an annual grant to a community organisation. Disclosure is not appointment or cessation evidence; exact tenure, pay, hours and leave unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Charitable trustee, patron or ambassador activity displayed separately and excluded from narrow employment headlines.

research_notes: Obtain appointment/payroll records giving exact dates, hours and leave for the UTS Students' Association Women's Officer role and determine whether it was paid employment.
Obtain exact title, employing department, appointment and cessation dates, hours and leave for the NSW Domestic Violence Unit role; resolve its overlap with Macquarie study.
Obtain dated employment records separating Bruce Childs and George Campbell service, including payroll titles, hours, leave, breaks and overlap with 1998 preselection/campaigning.
No public-sector duration is inferred from the undated NSW role. No private-sector employment is documented in the sources reviewed, but absence of evidence is not treated as zero.

2026-10-01 follow-up adds publisher-confirmed Upturn editorial activity, records UTS/masters sequence discrepancies and government-unit formation context, and removes unsupported Campbell-office election-day cessation.

Searched university/alumni/event transcripts, first-job and retail references, explicit hours/pay terms, ministerial/parliamentary biographies, historical CEDAW material and publisher/launch records. No dependable appointment dates, ordinary hours or leave found. A social-media commenter’s suggested UTS year is not treated as a personnel record. First-person UTS transcript confirms duties but no pay or tenure.

Next leads: contemporaneous UTS Students’ Association election/payroll and Vertigo archives; Macquarie graduation and NSW unit appointment records; separate Childs/Campbell payroll chronology; publishing contract/royalty disclosures and newspaper contribution terms. UN and Evatt retrospective article direct retrieval failed, while relevant indexed institutional text was available. No third-party worker’s hours are attributed to Plibersek.

Second follow-up2October2026: targeted UTS/Vertigo archive, Women’s Officer pay/year, Macquarie completion, domestic-violence-unit appointment and Childs-office chronology queries did not yield defensible dates or hours. Inside Story14March2023 biography review (https://insidestory.org.au/jane-austens-prime-minister/) describes the women’s-officer role as during honours, a useful possible explanation of previously conflicting degree/office sequence; retain as a lead pending contemporary student-association records, not proof of a1992 or1993 appointment. Crikey29January2004 delegate table labels the government role professional officer (https://www.crikey.com.au/2004/01/29/the-whos-who-of-national-conference/) without dates or payroll confirmation. Tim Ayres13June2023 tribute confirms Childs service in her early twenties but cannot date it precisely. No new bounded paid employment, leave or full-time evidence. Preserve existing facts and prioritize original student-association and public-service/personnel records over repeated broad biographies.

Third follow-up3October2026: targeted UTS repository/archive, 1992 Women’s Officer and Childs chronology searches found no contemporary student-association election, payroll or appointment record. A Facebook search snippet claims 1992 but is an uncertain recollection and is not adopted; the existing UTS honours completion remains 1993. Australian Women’s Register and Crikey results repeat already recorded role sequence/title evidence without dates or hours. Childs’s later parliamentary service endpoint is not substituted for Plibersek’s personal staff cessation. No substantive career fact changed.

Fourth follow-up4October2026: a directly accessible February2009 South Sydney Herald profile materially refines the NSW role to domestic-violence research and creation of publications and confirms the transition sequence into Bruce Childs's staff. It does not supply payroll title, appointment boundary, hours or leave. Fresh UTS repository, student-handbook and exact senator-office searches otherwise returned unrelated academic PDFs, existing secondary chronology and no personnel record; the 10September1997 end of Childs's Senate service remains only an outer bound, not Plibersek's personal cessation date.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Original 47th-Parliament interests declaration adds Jessie Street Trust trusteeship, CLAN patronage and Life Education NSW ambassadorship, separately excluded charitable roles. It also establishes personal publication royalties donated to Wayside Chapel and Exodus Foundation, but the publication is unnamed; Upturn remuneration remains unconfirmed and no royalty receipt is converted into a work interval. Current Vertigo web archive did not expose a1990s election/payroll record. Original PDF text available; screenshot restricted-URL errors were individual-source gaps, not terminal.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Primary June2007 House committee report materially supplies two approved parliamentary maternity-leave windows in2001/2005. Attendance leave is not cessation of membership or proven cessation of all duties; narrow headline totals unchanged. Publication-credit/year-specific NSW unit searches cross-checked with both engines did not identify a1990s authored publication or personal appointment; unit formation and senator term dates remain organisational outer context. No private PR consultancy is adopted from an inconsistent foreign-language derivative biography. Seek actual student-association payroll/NSW appointment and publication contracts for unresolved employment; original HTML restricted retrieval recovered via official report PDF.
